question: Which organ of the human body pumps blood?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Heart**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **heart** is a muscular organ located in the chest cavity.
 
• It is responsible for **pumping blood** throughout the body via the circulatory system.
 
• The heart ensures the continuous supply of **oxygen and nutrients** to tissues and organs.
 
• The heart operates through a series of **rhythmic contractions**, regulated by electrical impulses.
 
• It consists of four chambers: the **right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium,** and **left ventricle**.
 
• The heart's activity is vital for maintaining **homeostasis** and supporting life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pancreas**__

 __
 
• The **pancreas** is a gland located behind the stomach.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **digestive and endocrine functions**.
 
• The pancreas produces **digestive enzymes** and hormones such as **insulin**.
 
 
 
• **Stomach**__
 __
 
• The **stomach** is a muscular organ involved in the **digestion of food**.
 
• It secretes **gastric juices** that aid in breaking down food.
 
• The stomach's environment is highly **acidic**, which helps in killing harmful bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Liver**__
 
 
• The **liver** is a vital organ located in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen.
 
• It performs various functions including **detoxification, protein synthesis,** and production of **bile**.
 
• The liver also plays a role in **metabolism** and regulation of **blood sugar levels**.
